headline: Morgan Stanley analysts said SpaceX shares look "cheap and getting cheaper" compared with the company's growth, and the stock rose sharply on Monday.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: an analyst note moved one newly listed stock, with the price target unchanged at $300.
importance_line: SpaceX shareholders saw a jump of more than 5% on one bank's view, and the rise may also reflect Elon Musk's remarks about chip talks with TSMC, so it is an opinion, not a change in the company's results.
summary: Investopedia reports that SpaceX shares rose more than 5% on Monday, to levels not seen since July, after Morgan Stanley analysts wrote that, adjusted for growth, the Elon Musk-led company is "one of the cheaper ways" to play the space and intelligence economy. Morgan Stanley kept its "overweight" rating (it expects the shares to beat the market) and its $300 price target, well above the roughly $167 share price, while another report of the note on Yahoo Finance says the analysts also listed risks such as slower progress on Starship rocket reuse and extra funding needs.
notes: Investopedia page blocked (HTTP 402); text read on its AOL.ca copy (https://www.aol.ca/articles/spacex-stock-surges-morgan-stanley-165453000.html). Investopedia says the note came a day before Monday's rise; Chosunbiz reports a 7.63% close and says Musk's remarks about TSMC chip talks also lifted the stock. Analyst opinion. Original Investopedia link kept as url.
